answer: Borrow poker's chip-dumping checks: pair random seats in zero-sum duels, one drafting a hard puzzle, the other solving it, with points passing to the winner. Each seat also earns an Elo rating against strangers. When a pair's head-to-head results ripple far from what those ratings predict, like a strong solver who keeps losing to a weak setter so points drift one way like sand along a dune, both seats are merged into one reward share. Honest rivals bend like a willow but don't fold on cue.
